rubrics.justification: The response correctly recognizes a blastocyst-stage embryo and notes image limitations, but it overstates visibility of a compact ICM and cohesive TE. The image appears poorly expanded/collapsed with indistinct ICM and sparse hard-to-assess TE, so estimates like 3BB/4BB are likely too optimistic.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, BMI, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor context, and first-cycle status, and relates them appropriately to prognosis. Some points are somewhat generic and not tightly linked to the actual embryo morphology.

The structure is logical overall, but the implantation estimate seems high relative to the uncertain/possibly lower-quality morphology described from the image. There is some internal tension between acknowledging grading uncertainty and giving a fairly confident favorable prognosis.

Recommendations such as SET and standard luteal support are guideline-consistent, but suggesting ERA/mock cycle based on this case is not routine evidence-based practice, and PGT-A rationale is somewhat overstated for a 30-year-old first cycle. Overall mostly aligned with some deviations.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, lifestyle advice, review of embryo cohort, uterine cavity assessment if failure occurs, and male-factor workup. Some recommendations are broader than necessary for this favorable first-cycle case.
